chapter: Pranks, the Mingus fight and Duke's writing
title: Racism claims and Mingus's reliability
summary: Tizol and Rose deny he used racial slurs, and Willard says Mingus often invented prejudice.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, it's good to get the story of what really happened.
But that stuff about white folks and niggers, that's ridiculous.
No, I never used words like that.
Well, Mingus is famous for bringing issues up like that that never existed; I mean, he's always accusing people of being racially prejudice, when nobody said anything or did anything.
I don't believe I ever used the word 'nigger' in my whole life.
Juan just doesn't use that word.

But Charlie Mingus does. He's done that a lot of times, with people that work with him, and work for him, he's done the same thing, so ... Any time Mingus tells a story, I think it's good to get somebody else's version.
Right. In other words, he's prejudiced.
Yes, or, I think he tries to create, prejudice or turns the situation around where often there are not any; I've seen a couple of examples where he did that. You've read Mercer Ellington's book?
